clue.text: Water-carrying bags?

parts.note: bags is slang for trousers, so this reads as narrow tight trousers named after the pipes that carry rainwater off a roof

explanation.surface: A riddle about sacks used to carry water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for trousers; the answer names both the tubes that carry water and the very narrow trousers of 1950s Teddy boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight narrow-legged trousers were nicknamed after gutter tubes, which do carry water.

clue.text: Trooper oddly missing — that's a bit fishy

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the soldier word are dropped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: A soldier is absent, which seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly missing' removes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of TROOPER, leaving the 2nd, 4th and 6th.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs are a small part of a fish, hence a bit fishy.

clue.text: Layabout Bette's married off

indicators.note: off says this letter is taken away from the surname

parts.note: Bette Midler is the American singer and actress, so her surname is meant

explanation.surface: A singer has been married off and turned lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' removes M (married) from MIDLER, the surname of Bette Midler.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is an idle loafer, a synonym.

clue.text: Put basin right over the cat

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the vessel word above what follows

parts.note: a pan is a basin, as in a washing pan
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to tip a bowl over a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'over' stacks the basin word on top of the other two pieces, so it comes first in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard, especially a black one, is a big feline also called by this name.

clue.text: Dash and zap off couple of final letters

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word zap are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder
Z is the final letter of the alphabet, so a couple of them is two Zs

explanation.surface: Energy and zip are lost from the last two letters of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges ZAP to PZA; two Zs, the alphabet's last letter twice, are then added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and pizzazz both mean flamboyant style or vigour.

clue.text: Last month, in hospital, accepted fruit

indicators.note: in places the month abbreviation inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone in hospital last month took some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts ULT inside SAN; A (accepted) follows. ULT (ultimo) is old commercial shorthand for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedless dried white grape is a kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Blaine's wizardry embodies deception

indicators.note: embodies says the answer is contained within the run of words shown

explanation.surface: David Blaine's magic is just trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embodies' shows the answer sitting across 'BlaineS WIZardry'. David Blaine is an American street magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A swiz is British informal for a swindle or disappointing trick.

clue.text: Council hinders a new development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters grow into a different form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A council blocks a new building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' rearranges HINDERS A to SANHEDRI, and N (new) completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanhedrin was the supreme Jewish council and court in ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Angry about difficult men, pet? That's excessive

indicators.note: about places the angry word round the rearranged letters

parts.note: irate means angry

indicators.note: difficult implies the letters are awkward and need sorting, so men pet are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone cross with troublesome men calls it too much, love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' rearranges MEN PET to NTEMPE; 'about' wraps the angry word round it, splitting after its first letter. 'Pet' looks like an endearment addressed to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperate means immoderate, lacking self-restraint.

clue.text: … an earlier practitioner's nimbler with misdirection, take note

indicators.note: misdirection, the magician's trick, sends the letters astray: nimbler rearranged, less a note, is the answer
take means subtract here, so the note letter comes out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: Following on from Blaine, an older magician is quicker at misdirection.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 7 Across's magician Blaine. 'With misdirection' rearranges NIMBLER, from which 'take note' removes B, a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian wizard is an earlier practitioner of magic than a modern illusionist.

clue.text: Thoroughly sort out tangle with unfinished article

indicators.note: sort out signals putting these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Thoroughly untangling knots on an incomplete piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' rearranges TANGLE to ATLENG; 'unfinished' cuts the E from THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: At length can mean in full detail, exhaustively.

clue.text: Dear wife's home — so a superfluous instruction?

parts.note: cher is French for dear
chez la femme is French for at the woman's (wife's) home

explanation.surface: My dear, your wife is home, so there is no need to look for her.
explanation.walkthrough: The French saying means 'look for the woman'; if the wife is already home, telling someone to search for her is pointless, hence superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is an order to seek the woman behind a mystery, needless if she is known to be at home.

clue.text: Rising, I'm at work — work with regularly uppish animals

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
op is short for opus, a work
op again, short for opus

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word uppish

explanation.surface: Coming up in the world at my job, working with self-important animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes P, I, H from UPPISH; 'Rising' turns the whole string IMATOPOPPIH upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the large African river mammals, given in the plural.

clue.text: Backward-looking reviews for bar making no impression

indicators.note: backward-looking says the word is read from right to left

parts.note: recaps are summaries or reviews

explanation.surface: Nostalgic critiques for a pub that left no mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward-looking' turns RECAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar on a typewriter prints no character, so it leaves no impression on the page.

clue.text: Lays violently into boy-one not yet mature

indicators.note: into places the rearranged letters inside the boy's name

parts.note: Chris is a boy's name

indicators.note: violently signals the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a lad who is still immature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violently' rearranges LAYS to YSAL. 'Boy-one' reads as one word, but the hyphen just separates the boy from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is an insect not yet developed into its adult form.

clue.text: Peerage embarrassed bridge player? A shade

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
N, North, is one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A nobleman is mortified by his card partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassed' rearranges PEERAGE; N is North, a bridge position.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellowish green is a colour, or shade.

clue.text: Hull school?

definitions.meaning: the outer casing of seeds such as peas
a group of whales or dolphins

explanation.definitionFit: A pea's casing is its outer shell; a pod of dolphins is a group swimming together.

clue.text: Voracious fellow guzzling fruit? On the contrary

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so one word goes inside another
on the contrary reverses the roles, so the fruit swallows the fellow

parts.note: a gourd is a fruit
man means a fellow

explanation.surface: A greedy man stuffing himself with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guzzling' alone would put the fruit inside the fellow; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the fellow goes inside. 'Voracious' as an adjective is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it means greedy and excessively fond of eating.

clue.text: Stuffy head going bald

indicators.note: head going means the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: hairless means bald

explanation.surface: A stuffy man is losing his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head going' removes H, the first letter of HAIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A room without fresh air feels close and stuffy.

clue.text: British champion swallows mid-evening defeat

indicators.note: swallows places the middle letter inside the hero's name

parts.note: Ajax was a Greek hero, a champion of the Trojan War

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: A British hero takes a beating halfway through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid' takes N, the middle of EVENING; 'swallows' puts it inside AJAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Banjax is Irish slang for ruining or defeating someone or something.

clue.text: Curtain-fire caused by pub party down under

parts.note: a bar is a pub
rage is Australian slang for a party

explanation.surface: A pub party in Australia leads to a barrage of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' means Australia, where 'rage' means a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain of artillery fire laid down to protect troops is a classic barrage.

clue.text: Copper bends over Irishspeaking trio — time to be on the carpet!

indicators.note: to be on places the time letter before the carpet word

parts.note: to bow is to bend

indicators.note: Irish-speaking means the word for three is given as Irish speakers say it

parts.note: tri is Irish for three, said like the word tree
a runner is a long narrow carpet

explanation.surface: A policeman bows to three Irish speakers and is then reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first police force, founded in the 18th century. 'Irishspeaking' gives the sound of tri, Irish for three; 'to be on' puts the time letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: These officers were early London police, and copper is slang for a policeman.

clue.text: In context, Rachmaninoff is a minor player

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Rachmaninov, out of context, seems a lesser figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' shows the answer across 'contEXT RAchmaninoff'.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a walk-on performer with no lines.

clue.text: Assassin reporting an injury, a year gone

indicators.note: reporting signals the remaining letters are taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: from the letters of an injury take away A and YR (a year), leaving a sound like the answer in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: An assassin reports being hurt a year ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A year gone' removes A and YR (year) from AN INJURY; 'reporting' says the leftover NINJUR is heard, and in a British accent its final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese mercenaries trained in espionage and covert killing.

clue.text: Most advanced Listener puzzle I set with student

parts.note: an ear is the listening organ
L is for learner, a student

indicators.note: puzzle signals the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Listener crossword setter works with a student on the hardest puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard Times crossword, but here it just means an ear. 'Puzzle' rearranges I SET to IEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means first in time, so furthest forward or most advanced in date.

clue.text: Viola could be obsessive about Greek character

indicators.note: about places the fussy word round the Greek letter

parts.note: anal is informal for obsessively fussy
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A violist could be fanatical about a Greek figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viola' suggests the instrument or Shakespeare's heroine, but here it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden violas are often grown as plants completing their life cycle within one year.

clue.text: Hail falls in Namibia veldt

indicators.note: falls in says the answer drops inside the words following

explanation.surface: Hailstones come down on the African grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls in' shows the answer across 'NamibiA VEldt'. 'Hail' as weather is the trap; here it is a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is Latin for hail as a salutation, as in Ave Maria.

clue.text: Young woman, in extremis, Sabena …

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl, in dire straits, takes a Sabena flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' shows the answer across 'extreMIS Sabena'. Sabena was Belgium's national airline, which went bust in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a girl or unmarried young woman.

clue.text: … unexpectedly accepted as flight trainee

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests a surprise turn, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Continuing the airline story, someone is surprisingly taken on as a pilot trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the Sabena clue before it, so the surface pictures an airline taking on a pilot; 'unexpectedly' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is literally a trainee astronaut, one learning space flight.
